## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the inactive-`off` guard does what the description says. With no presentation flag, `omarchy-toggle-presentation off` returns before touching the bar, stay-awake or DND, including when repeated. The new regression test is meaningful: run against the script from 1382ed70 (before the guard), it fails at `inactive presentation off leaves an independently hidden bar`, and at this head all five checks pass. They also pass with current quattro's `omarchy-toggle-bar`. In isolated runs, bare `toggle` (the menu action), `status`, repeated `on`, and a start with only the bar already hidden also behaved correctly, and `omarchy toggle presentation` routes to the new script.

Three smaller state-restore gaps remain, described below.

### Presentation flag is created last, so an interrupted or overlapping `on` can lose the original state

`enable_presentation` writes the restore snapshot, changes the bar, DND and stay-awake, and only then creates the presentation flag (`bin/omarchy-toggle-presentation` lines 43-47). If `on` stops in between (for example Ctrl+C while `omarchy-shell` waits on a slow shell), the settings stay changed with no flag, and the new no-op `off` cannot undo them:

```text
start: bar visible, DND off, stay-awake off
on   write_restore (bar_off=0) -> bar hidden -> [interrupted before touch]
     state: bar hidden, no presentation flag
off  no flag -> returns early           bar stays hidden
on   snapshot now records bar_off=1
off  restores bar_off=1                 bar stays hidden
```

The same gap lets two overlapping `on` or `toggle` runs (a script racing a manual toggle, or a double-tapped custom keybinding) both pass the `enabled` check. The second run then rewrites the snapshot with values the first run already applied, and the later `off` leaves the bar hidden and DND on. This was reproduced by forcing the interleaving in an isolated run; it is unlikely from the menu, which closes before its action runs.

**Impact:** the user has to restore the bar (and possibly DND or stay-awake) by hand; no `on`/`off` sequence recovers the original state.

**Suggested change:** move `touch "$STATE_FILE"` to right after `write_restore`. With only that change, `off` after an interrupted `on` restored the visible bar, and a second `on` during the first returned early. That move narrows but does not close the overlap window, particularly for `toggle`. Serializing the whole script with `flock` on a lock file outside the watched `toggles/` directory, as `bin/omarchy-system-lock` already does, would cover it (the `flock` variant was not run).

### DND restore is silently dropped when the shell is unavailable

`disable_presentation` deletes the flag and snapshot (line 63) before calling `omarchy-shell -q notifications setDnd off` (line 69). With `-q`, `omarchy-shell` exits 0 on every failure (shell not running, not ready, or not responding), so the script cannot tell the call did nothing. The shell persists DND in `~/.local/state/omarchy/notifications.json`, so DND comes back on:

| After `on`, then `off` while the shell is down | Result |
|---|---|
| Bar, stay-awake (file flags) | Restored |
| DND (IPC only) | Stays on after the shell returns |
| A later `off` | No-op (no flag) |
| A later `on`/`off` pair | Snapshot records `dnd=on`, so DND is left on |

The `on` side has a related gap: `dnd_state` maps a failed `dndState` query to `off`, so starting presentation while the shell is not ready records `dnd=off`, and the later `off` clears a DND the user had on. Neither case is reachable from the menu (it runs inside the shell), only from the CLI, a keybinding or a script, for example in the seconds after login or a shell restart.

**Impact:** notifications can stay silenced after a presentation with no indication and no tool-level recovery.

**Suggested change:** call `setDnd off` without `-q` and check that it answers `off`. On failure, keep a DND-only pending marker (or leave the flag in place) and exit nonzero. In `dnd_state`, record `dnd=unknown` when the query fails and skip the DND restore for it.

### Stay-awake owned by a running `omarchy update` is removed mid-presentation

If presentation starts while an update holds stay-awake, `write_restore` records `stay_awake=1` and `omarchy-toggle-idle stay-awake` only `touch`es the file, so it keeps the update's owner token. When the update finishes, `omarchy-update-stay-awake stop` sees its token still in place and removes stay-awake while the presentation flag is still set. From the idle service source, the idle monitor is then re-enabled, so the screensaver and lock can start after the normal idle timeout during the rest of the presentation.

**Impact:** narrow timing, but per the idle service source the screensaver and lock can appear mid-presentation.

**Suggested change:** make one side ownership-aware, for example have `omarchy-update-stay-awake stop` leave stay-awake alone while `toggles/presentation` exists, or have presentation take over an update-owned file. This touches a file outside this PR, so a note or follow-up may fit better.

**Base note:** this branch predates quattro commit e1fc5022 ("Nudge the bar over IPC when toggling visibility"), whose message describes the toggles-directory watch stopping after flag changes land in quick succession. Presentation `on` and `off` each flip two flags there back to back. With current quattro's `omarchy-toggle-bar`, the nudge fires after each flip, so the outstanding desktop check is more representative on a rebased branch.

**Overlap note:** #12730 at d524068c carries the 1382ed70 script byte for byte, without this guard. If that PR is the one that lands, the guard and this regression test would still need to go with it.

**Documentation:** `manual/13-toggles-idle-screensaver.md` says toggle flags are named for the off state; `toggles/presentation` is named for the on state, so that sentence could note the exception.

**Test scope:** Reviewed at d66bb5ef. The PR test, the pre-guard negative control and additional scenarios ran in an isolated sandbox with a temporary home, real repository helpers for the bar, idle, toggle and update stay-awake scripts, and stubbed `omarchy-shell` and notification sending. Shell-down, interruption and overlapping-run cases are modeled with those stubs and forced interleavings; timing windows were not measured. On-screen results (bar, popups, idle lock) are inferred from the in-tree shell source; no desktop session or live shell was used. The full test suite was not rerun.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted cross-checks of each other's findings, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
